news.title: UEFA to boycott FIFA competitions after rejecting Gianni Infantino's investment plan; Concacaf also against
news.lede: UEFA said it and its 55 members will boycott FIFA competitions, rejecting FIFA's proposed plan to sell stakes to private investors, the European soccer governing body confirmed on Thursday. Concacaf, North America and the Caribbean's confederation, also publicly rejected the sell-off plan. This is a major update after Gianni Infantino officially announced on Tuesday his intention to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors by creating a new organization called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). Speaking to the official FIFA channels on Wednesday, Infantino insisted this is a "proposal, an offer, not an obligation.

news.title: Laura McAllister accuses FIFA of 'blackmail' over World Cup plan
news.lede: Laura McAllister is a former captain of the Wales women's football team. Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister has accused Fifa of trying to blackmail member associations into trying to accept its controversial private equity plan. European football's governing body has made a definitive stance against the Fifa proposals to sell stakes in major competitions. The position was backed up when Uefa's 55 member associations voted to boycott the World Cup in response.

news.title: Bayern Munich’s goalscorer Aleksandar Pavlović wants to move on from World Cup debacle after dominant friendly win
news.lede: Aleksandar Pavlović is choosing to look forward rather than dwell on Germany’s disappointing World Cup campaign. Reflecting on the tournament, the Bayern Munich midfielder made it clear that he is using the experience as motivation rather than allowing it to define him. “You have to take positives from every setback. Now I’m just looking forward to the season so I can show what I can do and achieve success with the team,” Pavlović said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia).

news.lede: Uefa’s constituent nations agreed to a boycott over Fifa’s plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup – a decision that, Miguel Delaney writes, could have ramifications right across the game. news.title: UEFA Votes 55-0 to Boycott All FIFA Competitions Over Private Equity World Cup Plan
news.lede: The Union of European Football Associations has voted unanimously to boycott future FIFA World Cups if the governing body follows up on its plan to sell stakes to private investors. As detailed in a statement released by UEFA on Thursday (July 30), the European governing body, which is one of FIFA’s six continental confederations for soccer, the 55 member associations voted unanimously to stand against FIFA’s proposed transfer of ownership interests in FIFA competitions, including the World Cup. “The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product,” reads the statement. “It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies.

news.title: UEFA will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino continues with plans to sell off stake in World Cup
news.lede: UEFA will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with his proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup. The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of all of UEFA's 55 member associations on Thursday afternoon, with a 55-0 vote. In a statement released on Thursday afternoon, UEFA said: "We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors." news.title: Fifa’s sales pitch revealed: more tournaments, more debt … but no mention of women’s game
news.lede: Fifa’s 25-page sales deck produced by JP Morgan. Reference made to doubling global tournaments. Fifa’s sales pitch to persuade members to approve the sale of the World Cup’s commercial rights clearly states that its plans for financial growth will be achieved by staging more tournaments, having higher ticket prices and debt financing. A 25-page sales deck titled “Fifa Forward Enterprise Member Materials”, that has been seen by the Guardian, makes the case for the creation of a new company to run Fifa’s commercial operations, 20% of which would be sold to Joshua Kushner, a US investor who is the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.
